title: Edge AI & Mobile Deployment
description: Edge AI: Device'ta (mobile, IoT) ML inference. TensorFlow Lite, CoreML, ONNX Runtime. On-device: Privacy (no cloud), low latency (<100ms), offline. Model compression (quantization, pruning) kritik.

content.level0_basic: Edge AI, ML inference'ı device'ta (smartphone, IoT, edge device) çalıştırır. Cloud'a data gönderme yok → privacy, offline çalışır. Örnek: Face unlock (iPhone, on-device), voice assistant wake word (local), real-time translation (Google Pixel). Avantajlar: (1) Privacy (data device'ta kalır). (2) Low latency (<50ms, cloud: 200-500ms network). (3) Offline (internet yok, çalışır). (4) Bandwidth (video stream cloud'a göndermek costly). Challenges: Limited compute (mobile CPU/GPU << server), limited memory (4-8GB RAM, <100MB model), battery (energy efficient). Framework: TensorFlow Lite (Android/iOS), CoreML (iOS), ONNX Runtime (cross-platform).
content.level1_beginner: Edge deployment pipeline: (1) **Train** cloud'da (PyTorch/TF, GPU). (2) **Optimize**: Quantization (FP32→INT8, 4x smaller), pruning (50-90% weights). (3) **Convert**: TFLite, CoreML, ONNX. Operator support check. (4) **Deploy**: Mobile app integrate (Java/Kotlin Android, Swift iOS). (5) **Inference**: On-device (<100ms). TFLite: Post-training quantization (PTQ), dynamic range, INT8. Delegates: GPU (fast), NNAPI (Android hardware), CoreML (iOS Neural Engine). Model size: <10MB ideal (app size), <50MB acceptable. Latency: <50ms real-time, <200ms acceptable. Frameworks karşılaştırma: TFLite (cross-platform, Google), CoreML (iOS only, Apple optimized), ONNX Runtime (flexible, Microsoft), PyTorch Mobile (experimental).
content.level2_application: Use cases: (1) **Computer Vision**: Object detection (YOLO, MobileNet), image classification (EfficientNet-Lite), segmentation. Real-time AR (Snapchat filters). (2) **NLP**: On-device translation (Google Pixel), keyboard prediction, voice assistant (wake word detection). (3) **Audio**: Speech recognition (Whisper-tiny), noise cancellation, music genre classification. (4) **Healthcare**: ECG analysis (wearables), sleep monitoring, fall detection (Apple Watch). (5) **Automotive**: ADAS (advanced driver assistance), lane detection, collision warning. Edge devices (cameras). (6) **IoT**: Smart home (security camera object detection), predictive maintenance (sensor data). Framework seçimi: Android → TFLite (GPU delegate), iOS → CoreML (Neural Engine), Cross-platform → ONNX Runtime. Optimization: MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-Lite (efficient architectures). Tools: TFLite Model Maker, Apple CreateML, ONNX Model Zoo.
content.level3_advanced: Advanced techniques: (1) **Hardware Acceleration**: Android NNAPI (Hexagon DSP, NPU), iOS CoreML (Neural Engine, GPU, ANE). Delegate selection (automatic, fallback CPU). (2) **Quantization Advanced**: QAT (quantization-aware training, <0.5% accuracy loss), per-channel quantization, mixed precision (critical layers FP16). (3) **Model Architecture**: MobileNetV3 (h-swish, squeeze-excite), EfficientNet-Lite (compound scaling), NAS-designed (MnasNet). Depthwise separable convolutions (parameter ↓). (4) **Optimization**: Operator fusion (conv+BN+ReLU), constant folding, layout optimization (NCHW vs NHWC). TFLite Converter optimizations. (5) **On-Device Training**: Federated learning (privacy-preserving), personalization (user-specific fine-tuning). Transfer learning (feature extraction frozen). (6) **Power Optimization**: INT8 (2-4x energy ↓), model caching (first run compile), batch processing. Thermal throttling aware. (7) **Edge TPU**: Google Coral (USB accelerator, 4 TOPS, INT8 only). Custom hardware (Raspberry Pi + accelerator).
content.level4_expert: Production deployment: (1) **A/B Testing**: Model versioning, gradual rollout (1% → 100%). Fallback (if inference fail, cloud API). (2) **Monitoring**: On-device metrics (latency p50/p99, memory, battery), crash analytics. Model performance (accuracy drift). (3) **Over-The-Air Updates**: Model update via app update (Play Store, App Store) or dynamic download (Firebase ML). Delta updates (model diff). (4) **Security**: Model encryption (prevent reverse engineering), secure enclave (biometric data). Adversarial robustness. (5) **Multi-Model**: Model cascade (fast screening → accurate, e.g., wake word → ASR). Model switching (day/night, battery level). (6) **Custom Ops**: TFLite custom operators (unsupported ops). Flex delegates (select TF ops). (7) **Neural Architecture Search**: Hardware-aware NAS (target device constraints). Latency, memory, energy optimization. Research: **TinyML** (MCU deployment, <1MB models, Arduino, STM32), **Neuromorphic hardware** (event-driven, ultra-low power), **Disaggregated inference** (split model: edge + cloud), **Privacy-preserving** (secure multi-party computation, homomorphic encryption).

whatIsIt: Edge AI: ML inference on edge devices (mobile, IoT). Local processing (no cloud). Matematiksel: Latency = T_inference + T_network (edge: T_network=0). Energy: E ∝ operations × power. Quantization: W_INT8 = round((W_FP32 - min) / (max - min) × 255) - 128. Model size: FP32 (4 bytes/param) → INT8 (1 byte) = 4x smaller. Throughput: FPS = 1 / T_inference. Constraints: Memory <100MB, latency <100ms, power <1W.
whyNeeded: Edge AI critical: (1) **Privacy**: Healthcare, finance data (HIPAA, GDPR). On-device → no cloud data leak. (2) **Latency**: Real-time (AR 16ms, voice <200ms). Cloud: 200-500ms network RTT. (3) **Offline**: Rural areas, airplanes, tunnels. No connectivity required. (4) **Bandwidth**: Video streams (GB/day). Edge processing → metadata only cloud. (5) **Cost**: Cloud inference $0.001-0.01 per request. Billions of users → expensive. Edge: one-time model. (6) **Reliability**: Network failures. Edge: autonomous. (7) **Scale**: Billions of devices (smartphones 6B+). Cloud can't handle all inference.
realWorldAnalogy: Edge AI'ı lokal restoran vs cloud kitchen'a benzetebiliriz. **Cloud (cloud kitchen)**: Sipariş ver (data upload), uzak mutfak pişir (inference cloud GPU), delivery (result download). Yavaş (30-60 min latency), pahalı (delivery fee), açık olmalı (online). **Edge (lokal restoran/home cooking)**: Kendi mutfak (device), hemen pişir (inference local). Hızlı (<5 min), free (no delivery), offline (market kapalı olsa da). Trade-off: Lokal mutfak küçük (limited hardware), basit yemekler (compressed model). Cloud mutfak büyük (data center GPU), complex yemekler (large models). **Privacy**: Home cooking → recipe secret (data private). Cloud kitchen → recipe paylaş (privacy concern). **Cost**: Home cooking → initial setup (stove, oven = model deployment), sonra free. Cloud → her sipariş ücret (per-request cost). Edge AI: Initial investment (model optimization), sonra scale free.

formulas: \text{Energy}: \quad E = P \cdot T \quad \text{(power × time, mW × ms = mJ)}

stepByStep: 1. **Model Selection**: Task (classification, detection, segmentation). Accuracy vs size/speed trade-off. Mobile-optimized: MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-Lite, YOLO-nano. Baseline: Train/validate on cloud.

2. **Optimization**: (a) Quantization: TFLite PTQ (FP32→INT8, representative dataset 100-1000 samples). (b) Pruning: 50-70% sparsity (structured, channel pruning). (c) Knowledge distillation: Teacher → student (smaller). Target: <10MB model, <1% accuracy loss.

3. **Conversion**: (a) TensorFlow → TFLite (.tflite). (b) PyTorch → ONNX → TFLite/CoreML. (c) Check operator support (unsupported → custom ops or replace). (d) Validate: Compare outputs (original vs converted, numerical precision).

4. **Hardware Target**: (a) Android: NNAPI delegate (NPU, DSP), GPU delegate (OpenCL, Vulkan). (b) iOS: CoreML (Neural Engine A11+, GPU, CPU). (c) Edge device: Coral TPU (INT8 only), Jetson (NVIDIA). Select delegate (benchmark latency).

5. **Mobile Integration**: (a) Android: Add TFLite dependency (build.gradle), load model (Interpreter), run inference (ByteBuffer input/output). (b) iOS: Add CoreML model, MLModel wrapper, predict. (c) Preprocessing: Image resize, normalize (same as training). (d) Postprocessing: Decode outputs (bounding boxes, class labels).

6. **Performance Optimization**: (a) Model caching: First run compile (AOT), cache. (b) Thread count: interpreter.setNumThreads(4). (c) Batch processing: Multiple inputs (amortize overhead). (d) Quantization: INT8 (2-4x faster, 4x smaller). (e) Resolution: Lower input size (224x224 → 160x160, speed ↑, accuracy ↓).

7. **Testing**: (a) Latency: Measure on target device (real hardware, not emulator). p50, p99 percentiles. (b) Memory: Peak memory usage (profiler). (c) Accuracy: Test set evaluation (original vs on-device). (d) Battery: Power profiler (Android Battery Historian, iOS Instruments). (e) Thermal: Long-running (thermal throttling?).

8. **Deployment**: (a) Package: App bundle with model (.tflite, .mlmodel). (b) Size: Model <10MB (app size limit 150MB iOS). (c) Versioning: Model version tracking. (d) Rollout: Gradual (A/B test, 1% → 100%). (e) Fallback: If on-device fail → cloud API (network available).

9. **Monitoring**: (a) Latency metrics: p50, p99 (Firebase Performance Monitoring). (b) Crash analytics: Model inference crashes. (c) Accuracy drift: Sample predictions → cloud validation. (d) User feedback: In-app feedback. (e) Device distribution: CPU, OS versions (optimize for popular devices).

10. **Updates**: (a) OTA (over-the-air): Firebase ML Model Management, dynamic model download (update without app update). (b) Delta updates: Model diff (only changed weights). (c) Versioning: Backward compatible. (d) A/B testing: New model vs old (champion/challenger). (e) Rollback: If new model bad → revert.
algorithm.complexity: **Inference Time**: Mobile CPU: 50-200ms (MobileNetV3), GPU: 20-50ms, Neural Engine (iOS): 10-30ms. Edge TPU: 5-10ms (INT8 only). **Model Size**: FP32: 10-50MB typical. INT8: 2.5-12.5MB (4x smaller). <10MB ideal (app size). **Memory**: Model + activations. MobileNet: 10-30MB runtime. Larger models (ResNet-50): 100-200MB. **Energy**: INT8: 2-4x less energy vs FP32. Inference: 50-500mJ per frame (varies by model, hardware). **Scalability**: Billions of devices (smartphones 6B+). Edge: Distributed (each device local), no server bottleneck. Cloud: Centralized (expensive, bandwidth).

codeExamples.title: TensorFlow Lite Conversion
codeExamples.code:
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

# Train model (simplified)
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(32, 3, activation='relu', input_shape=(224, 224, 3)),
    tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling2D(),
    tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(64, 3, activation='relu'),
    tf.keras.layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])

model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='categorical_crossentropy')
print(f'Model parameters: {model.count_params():,}')

# Convert to TFLite (FP32)
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(model)
tflite_model = converter.convert()

with open('model.tflite', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(tflite_model)

print(f'\nFP32 TFLite size: {len(tflite_model)/1024:.1f} KB')

# Post-Training Quantization (INT8)
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(model)
converter.optimizations = [tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT]

# Representative dataset for calibration
def representative_dataset():
    for _ in range(100):
        yield [np.random.randn(1, 224, 224, 3).astype(np.float32)]

converter.representative_dataset = representative_dataset
converter.target_spec.supported_ops = [tf.lite.OpsSet.TFLITE_BUILTINS_INT8]
converter.inference_input_type = tf.uint8
converter.inference_output_type = tf.uint8

tflite_quant_model = converter.convert()

with open('model_quant.tflite', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(tflite_quant_model)

print(f'INT8 TFLite size: {len(tflite_quant_model)/1024:.1f} KB')
print(f'Compression: {len(tflite_model)/len(tflite_quant_model):.1f}x smaller')
print('\nDeploy to Android/iOS app!')
codeExamples.explanation: TFLite Conversion: FP32 → INT8 (PTQ). 4x smaller, 2-4x faster. Representative dataset (calibration). Deploy mobile app.

codeExamples.title: TFLite Inference (Python)
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import time

# Load TFLite model
interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_path='model_quant.tflite')
interpreter.allocate_tensors()

# Get input/output details
input_details = interpreter.get_input_details()
output_details = interpreter.get_output_details()

print('Input details:')
print(f"  Shape: {input_details[0]['shape']}")
print(f"  Type: {input_details[0]['dtype']}")

print('\nOutput details:')
print(f"  Shape: {output_details[0]['shape']}")
print(f"  Type: {output_details[0]['dtype']}")

# Prepare input
input_shape = input_details[0]['shape']
input_data = np.random.randint(0, 255, input_shape, dtype=np.uint8)

# Inference
interpreter.set_tensor(input_details[0]['index'], input_data)

start = time.time()
interpreter.invoke()
latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000

output_data = interpreter.get_tensor(output_details[0]['index'])

print(f'\nInference latency: {latency:.2f} ms')
print(f'Output shape: {output_data.shape}')
print(f'Predictions (top 3): {np.argsort(output_data[0])[-3:][::-1]}')

# Benchmark (100 runs)
latencies = []
for _ in range(100):
    start = time.time()
    interpreter.invoke()
    latencies.append((time.time() - start) * 1000)

print(f'\nBenchmark (100 runs):')
print(f'  Mean: {np.mean(latencies):.2f} ms')
print(f'  p50: {np.percentile(latencies, 50):.2f} ms')
print(f'  p99: {np.percentile(latencies, 99):.2f} ms')
codeExamples.explanation: TFLite Inference: Load model (Interpreter), allocate tensors, set input, invoke, get output. Benchmark: p50, p99 latency. Mobile: Java/Kotlin (Android), Swift (iOS).

codeExamples.title: CoreML Conversion (iOS)
codeExamples.code:
import coremltools as ct
import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

# Load TF model
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(32, 3, activation='relu', input_shape=(224, 224, 3)),
    tf.keras.layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])

model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='categorical_crossentropy')

print('Converting to CoreML...')

# Convert to CoreML
mlmodel = ct.convert(
    model,
    inputs=[ct.ImageType(name='input', shape=(1, 224, 224, 3))],
    outputs=[ct.TensorType(name='output')],
    convert_to='mlprogram'  # Or 'neuralnetwork'
)

# Add metadata
mlmodel.short_description = 'Image classifier'
mlmodel.author = 'Your Name'
mlmodel.license = 'MIT'

# Save
mlmodel.save('ImageClassifier.mlpackage')

print(f'CoreML model saved: ImageClassifier.mlpackage')
print(f'Model size: ~{model.count_params() * 4 / 1024 / 1024:.1f} MB (FP32)')

# Quantization (INT8)
mlmodel_quant = ct.models.neural_network.quantization_utils.quantize_weights(
    mlmodel, nbits=8
)
mlmodel_quant.save('ImageClassifier_quant.mlpackage')

print(f'Quantized model saved (8-bit)')
print('\nDeploy to iOS app (Xcode)!')
print('Usage: let model = try ImageClassifier(configuration: MLModelConfiguration())')
codeExamples.explanation: CoreML Conversion: TensorFlow/PyTorch → CoreML (.mlpackage). Quantization (8-bit). iOS: Neural Engine (fast), GPU. Swift/Objective-C integration.

codeExamples.title: Edge TPU Deployment (Coral)
codeExamples.code:
# Install: pip install pycoral tflite-runtime
from pycoral.utils import edgetpu
from pycoral.adapters import common
from pycoral.adapters import classify
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import time

# Edge TPU requires INT8 quantized model with specific ops
model_path = 'model_edgetpu.tflite'  # Compiled for Edge TPU

print('Initializing Edge TPU...')
interpreter = edgetpu.make_interpreter(model_path)
interpreter.allocate_tensors()

print(f'Edge TPU initialized: {interpreter._delegates}')

# Load image
image = Image.open('test.jpg').resize((224, 224))
input_data = np.array(image, dtype=np.uint8)[np.newaxis, ...]

# Inference
common.set_input(interpreter, input_data)

start = time.time()
interpreter.invoke()
latency = (time.time() - start) * 1000

output = common.output_tensor(interpreter, 0)

print(f'\nInference latency: {latency:.2f} ms (Edge TPU)')
print(f'Top prediction: class {np.argmax(output)}, confidence {np.max(output):.2f}')

# Benchmark
latencies = []
for _ in range(100):
    start = time.time()
    interpreter.invoke()
    latencies.append((time.time() - start) * 1000)

print(f'\nBenchmark (100 runs):')
print(f'  Mean: {np.mean(latencies):.2f} ms')
print(f'  Min: {np.min(latencies):.2f} ms')
print(f'  Max: {np.max(latencies):.2f} ms')
print('\nEdge TPU: 4 TOPS, INT8 only, USB accelerator ($60)')
print('Use case: Raspberry Pi, embedded systems, low-power edge')
codeExamples.explanation: Edge TPU (Coral): Google USB accelerator (4 TOPS). INT8 only. Compile model (edgetpu_compiler). Ultra-fast (5-10ms). Raspberry Pi, embedded.

codeExamples.title: Model Performance Comparison
codeExamples.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Simulate model comparison (size, latency, accuracy)
models = ['MobileNetV3-Small', 'MobileNetV3-Large', 'EfficientNet-Lite0', 'EfficientNet-Lite4', 'ResNet-50']

# Model size (MB)
sizes = [2.5, 5.5, 4.0, 13.0, 98.0]

# Latency (ms) on mobile CPU
latencies = [15, 30, 25, 80, 250]

# Accuracy (top-1 ImageNet, %)
accuracies = [67.4, 75.2, 75.1, 81.5, 76.1]

# Plot
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4))

# Size
ax = axes[0]
ax.bar(models, sizes, color='skyblue')
ax.set_ylabel('Model Size (MB)')
ax.set_title('Model Size Comparison')
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax.axhline(10, color='r', linestyle='--', label='10MB target')
ax.legend()

# Latency
ax = axes[1]
ax.bar(models, latencies, color='lightcoral')
ax.set_ylabel('Latency (ms)')
ax.set_title('Inference Latency (Mobile CPU)')
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax.axhline(50, color='r', linestyle='--', label='50ms target')
ax.legend()

# Accuracy
ax = axes[2]
ax.bar(models, accuracies, color='lightgreen')
ax.set_ylabel('Accuracy (%)')
ax.set_title('ImageNet Top-1 Accuracy')
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print('=== Mobile Model Comparison ===')
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f'{model}:')
    print(f'  Size: {sizes[i]} MB, Latency: {latencies[i]} ms, Accuracy: {accuracies[i]}%')

print('\nRecommendation:')
print('  Real-time (<50ms): MobileNetV3-Small/Large, EfficientNet-Lite0')
print('  High accuracy: EfficientNet-Lite4 (tradeoff latency)')
print('  Avoid: ResNet-50 (too slow for mobile)')
codeExamples.explanation: Model Comparison: Size vs latency vs accuracy. Mobile-optimized: MobileNet, EfficientNet-Lite. Trade-offs: Speed ↔ accuracy. Target: <10MB, <50ms.

quiz.explanation: Edge: (1) Privacy (data local), (2) Latency (no network), (3) Offline (no internet), (4) Bandwidth (no upload), (5) Cost (scale free). Trade-off: Limited compute/memory.

commonMistakes.why: FP32: 4x larger, 2-4x slower, 2-4x more energy. Mobile storage/battery limited. App size bloat.
commonMistakes.fix: Always quantize: PTQ (FP32 → INT8). TFLite converter (representative dataset). <1% accuracy loss, 4x compression. QAT for <0.5% loss.

commonMistakes.why: Emulator: Desktop CPU (fast, not representative). Real device: Mobile CPU/GPU (slower, thermal throttling). Latency mismatch (10x difference possible).
commonMistakes.fix: Test on real devices: Mid-range phones (not flagship only). Measure p50, p99 latency. Profile: Battery, thermal. Device distribution (optimize for popular).

commonMistakes.why: CPU only: 100-300ms. GPU delegate: 20-50ms (5x faster). NNAPI/Neural Engine: 10-30ms (10x faster). Missing huge speedup.
commonMistakes.fix: Enable delegates: TFLite GPU delegate (Android), CoreML Neural Engine (iOS), NNAPI. Benchmark: CPU vs GPU vs NPU. Fallback CPU (unsupported ops).

commonMistakes.why: App size limit (iOS 150MB). Download slow (cellular data). Storage limited. User uninstall (large apps).
commonMistakes.fix: Target <10MB: Quantization (4x), pruning (2-3x), distillation (5-10x). Architecture: MobileNet, EfficientNet-Lite. OTA download (not bundled).

commonMistakes.why: Image preprocessing: Resize, normalize, color convert. Naive: 50-100ms (bottleneck!). Inference: 20ms. Total: 70-120ms (preprocessing dominant).
commonMistakes.fix: Optimize preprocessing: (1) Hardware accelerate (GPU, NEON), (2) Batch processing, (3) Lower resolution (224→160, if acceptable), (4) Pre-resize camera (not full res).

commonMistakes.why: On-device inference fail (OOM, unsupported ops, thermal throttling). App crash or stuck. Bad user experience.
commonMistakes.fix: Fallback: (1) Cloud API (if network available), (2) Simpler model (switch to smaller), (3) Graceful degradation (disable feature). Error handling, retry logic.

commonMistakes.why: Continuous inference (camera, audio): Battery drain. User complaints, negative reviews. Thermal throttling (device hot).
commonMistakes.fix: Power optimization: (1) INT8 (2-4x less energy), (2) Inference throttling (not every frame, e.g., 10 FPS), (3) Sleep mode (idle detection), (4) Batch processing (amortize overhead).
